solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Food shop with decent sales, I suspect (12)

indicatorNotes.suspect: what you suspect is not what it seems: the letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A shopkeeper guesses their takings have been respectable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' reads as a shrug tacked onto the sentence, but 'suspect' is the working word and 'I' is a letter of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared and fine foods.

entries.clue: This is what soldiers might get up to (8)

annotation.definition: This is what soldiers might get up to

blocks.note: the thing soldiers respond to: an army signal, not an activity
the surface hears mischief; the setter means rising from bed to a call

annotation.surface: A hint of barrack-room mischief: what squaddies get up to when nobody is looking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get up to' suggests misbehaviour, but here it is literal: soldiers get up to the sound of reveille.
annotation.definitionFit: Reveille is the signal played to rouse soldiers in the morning, so they rise to it.

entries.clue: Drink that’s essential for Christmas-time (4)

indicatorNotes.essential for: the answer is in the essence, the inside, of the words that follow

blocks.note: the four letters straddling the hyphen, at the heart of the phrase

annotation.surface: A festive claim that one particular drink is a must at Christmas.
annotation.walkthrough: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, a crossword regular; the hyphen in 'Christmas-time' does not stop the letters running on.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont.

entries.clue: Claim stage is covered in beer (6)

indicatorNotes.is covered in: one piece sits inside another, wrapped by it

blocks.note: ale is a beer; it goes round the outside
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

annotation.surface: Someone asserts a theatre stage has been swamped with beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stage' pulls toward the theatre, but it is a stage of a journey: a leg.
annotation.definitionFit: To allege is to claim something without proof.

entries.clue: Fight debt a lot after messing up (2,6)

indicatorNotes.after messing up: the letters come out after being messed up: jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Someone who has made a mess of their finances must now struggle with heavy debt.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'messing up' the cause of the debt; in fact it acts on 'debt a lot'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: the phrase is a slightly formal way of saying engage in combat.

entries.clue: Hairy creature one’s pursuing still (4)

indicatorNotes.pursuing: one piece chases the other, so comes after it

blocks.note: still = yet, as in 'yet more'
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Some shaggy beast is still being hunted by somebody.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' is 'one is': the I is pursuing, so placed after, YET. The yeti is the abominable snowman of Himalayan legend.
annotation.definitionFit: The yeti is said to be a large, shaggy ape-like creature.

entries.clue: Fifty-fifty chance rugby match doesn’t start (5)

indicatorNotes.doesn’t start: the word loses its starting letter

blocks.note: sevens is the seven-a-side form of rugby
SEVENS without its first letter

annotation.surface: A rugby match is postponed, so whether it happens is a coin toss.
annotation.walkthrough: Rugby sevens is a short, fast game with seven players a side, and a tournament of it is simply called sevens.
annotation.definitionFit: Betting at evens means an even-money, fifty-fifty chance.

entries.clue: Female bringing up young with pride? (7)

annotation.definition: Female bringing up young with pride?

blocks.note: a mother raising her offspring
the surface hears a feeling; a pride is also the collective noun for a group of big cats

annotation.surface: A proud mother raising her children.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With pride' sounds like a mother's feeling; the question mark flags the collective noun for lions.
annotation.definitionFit: A lioness raises her cubs within the pride.

entries.clue: Expose affair in entertainment industry (4,8)

blocks.note: to expose is to show
an affair is a matter or business, as in 'that's my affair'

annotation.surface: A newspaper uncovers a celebrity's affair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Affair' reads as a romance in the surface; here it means a matter, business.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the phrase covers theatre, film and television as a trade.

entries.clue: Object I briefly see in catalogue (7)

indicatorNotes.briefly: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: an item is an object
as written
SEE with its last letter dropped

annotation.surface: A shopper spots something they want in a mail-order catalogue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catalogue' looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the verb: to list item by item.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: both mean listing things one entry at a time.

entries.clue: In the morning I leave Madrileno friend (5)

blocks.note: a.m. = in the morning
as written
to leave is to go

annotation.surface: A traveller says goodbye to a friend in Madrid one morning.
annotation.walkthrough: A Madrileño is a native of Madrid, so the definition asks for the Spanish word for friend.
annotation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, the word someone from Madrid would use.

entries.clue: Leased piece of land where Swedes may put down roots? (9)

annotation.definition2: where Swedes may put down roots?

blocks.note: a small plot rented from the council for growing food

blocks.clueFragment: where Swedes may put down roots?
blocks.note: a swede is a turnip-like root vegetable, planted in a rented garden plot

annotation.surface: Scandinavian immigrants settle down on rented land.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S makes 'Swedes' look like people from Sweden; a swede is also a turnip-like root vegetable, which grows on an allotment, a small rented garden plot common in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: An allotment is a plot of land rented out for growing vegetables.

entries.clue: Experimental equipment in trial underground (4,4)

blocks.note: a trial is a test
the Tube is London's underground railway

annotation.surface: A trial of some experimental kit is run on the Underground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Tube' is the everyday name for the London Underground.
annotation.definitionFit: A test tube is basic laboratory equipment for experiments.

entries.clue: Replacement taking public transport back (3)

blocks.note: a bus is public transport

annotation.surface: A replacement bus service brings passengers home.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a rail replacement bus; the definition is a substitute player.
annotation.definitionFit: A short form: the answer clips substitute, as in a player coming off the bench.

entries.clue: MP’s niece somehow becoming a model (8)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters are rearranged in some way or other

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A politician's niece has somehow become a fashion model.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A model' is not a fashion model but an example, a representative sample.
annotation.definitionFit: Model in the sense of a typical example, a sample representing its kind, not a person posing.

entries.clue: Watch yours truly being caught (3)

indicatorNotes.being caught: caught by the ear: what is heard

blocks.note: yours truly = the speaker, I

annotation.surface: A speaker is spotted, perhaps caught on camera.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' suggests being spotted; here it means caught by the ear. 'Yours truly' is a jokey way to say me, so I.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to look at closely or keep an eye on.

entries.clue: Feeble son stupidly sleeps in (9)

indicatorNotes.stupidly: the letters are arranged stupidly: jumbled

blocks.note: s = son, as in genealogies
anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A parent grumbles that their weak son is lying in bed late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sleeps in' looks like a lazy lie-in; both words are fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Spineless means lacking backbone, weak and feeble.

entries.clue: Is tragic king overthrown in Middle Eastern country? (6)

indicatorNotes.overthrown: thrown over, turned upside down: in a down clue the word reads upwards

blocks.note: as written
King Lear, Shakespeare's tragedy

annotation.surface: A question about a doomed monarch being deposed in the Middle East.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overthrown' fits a king in the surface, and it is exactly what happens to LEAR's letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is a state on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

entries.clue: Rent place in Croatia (5)

blocks.note: rent = torn apart, the past tense of rend
a port city on the Dalmatian coast

annotation.surface: Someone looking to rent somewhere to stay in Croatia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like letting property, but it is the past participle of rend: torn apart.
annotation.definitionFit: Rent, as in torn, means split; Split is also a Croatian port city.

entries.clue: Music producer’s stolen money, I hear (4)

indicatorNotes.I hear: the answer is what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: loot is stolen goods or money

annotation.surface: Gossip that a record producer's cash was stolen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a person in a studio; a lute is an instrument, which produces music. The 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A lute is a stringed instrument, so it produces music.

entries.clue: Penniless old German — or someone from Moscow? (7)

indicatorNotes.Penniless: without a penny: P is taken away

blocks.note: Prussia was a former German state
PRUSSIAN losing its P, for penny

annotation.surface: A question about the nationality of a poor émigré: German, or Russian?
annotation.walkthrough: P is the standard abbreviation for penny.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a Muscovite is one particular kind of citizen of that country.

entries.clue: Charlie infiltrating established faith community (4)

blocks.note: set = established, as in set in stone; it goes round the outside
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone called Charlie worms their way into a long-standing religious group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a person's name; it is the radio code word for C.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a group sharing religious beliefs, often split from a larger church.

entries.clue: Remarkable reason for not eating? (7)

blocks.note: worth remarking on, worthy of attention
the answer split 2,5: having nowhere to sit down for a meal

annotation.surface: Someone gives an unusual excuse for skipping a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split: NOTABLE read as NO TABLE, a restaurant turning you away.
annotation.definitionFit: Notable means worthy of notice, remarkable.

entries.clue: Musical game with many moving pieces (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Musical' is used as a noun: a stage musical

blocks.note: a 1980s stage show by Tim Rice and the ABBA songwriters
a board game of kings, queens and pawns

annotation.surface: A board game whose many parts dance about to music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like an adjective describing the game; it is a noun, the name of a show.
annotation.definitionFit: Chess is both a musical and a board game played with moving pieces.
